name: Big Works Pty Ltd
narrative: On 29 May 2026 a Compliance Notice was issued to Big Works Pty Ltd under section 73ZM of the National Disability Insurance Scheme Act 2013 (NDIS Act). The notice requires Big Works Pty Ltd to take certain action to address non-compliance with section 73J of the NDIS Act due to failing to comply with a condition of registration, specifically section 73F(2)(b), a condition that the person comply with the NDIS Code of Conduct rules and section 73F(2)(c), all applicable standards and other requirements of the NDIS Practice Standards. The compliance notice relates to NDIS Code of Conduct Rules relating to a requirement that a “Code-covered person must provide supports and services in a safe and competent manner, with care and skill” and “In providing supports or services a code covered person must: act with integrity, honesty and transparency”, and to the NDIS (Provider Registration and Practice Standards) Rules relating to responsive support provision “Each participant can access responsive, timely, competent and appropriate supports to meet their needs, desired outcomes and goals”, “Each participant’s support needs are met by workers who are competent in relation to their role, hold relevant qualifications and have relevant expertise and experience to provide person-centred support” and “Each participant experiences a planned and coordinated transition to or from the provider”.

More specifically, Dash Group Pty Ltd trading as Dash Group is required by 22 April 2026 to take action to engage an approved quality auditor to complete a condition audit in accordance with conditions of registration imposed under section 73G section of the National Disability Insurance Scheme Act 2013 and by 27 June 2026 to provide the NDIS Commission a copy of the completed conditional audit report. Date and time of effect: 30 March 2026 from 5:00pmThe compliance notice was issued on the basis that a delegate of the Commissioner was aware of information that suggests Dash Group Pty Ltd trading as Dash Group, has contravened section 73J of the NDIS Act, by allegedly failing to commence a condition audit within 3 months of commencing service in any of the classes of support that require certification assessment and as part of the stage 1 audit, provide the approved quality auditor with revised self-assessment responses against the applicable NDIS Practice Standards.Status

More specifically, T Dube & K.L Modise trading as TAMBA HEALTHCARE is required by 22 April 2026 to take action to engage an approved quality auditor to complete a condition audit in accordance with conditions of registration imposed under section 73G section of the National Disability Insurance Scheme Act 2013 and by 27 June 2026 to provide the NDIS Commission a copy of the completed conditional audit report.The compliance notice was issued on the basis that a delegate of the Commissioner was aware of information that suggests T Dube & K.L Modise trading as TAMBA HEALTHCARE, has contravened section 73J of the NDIS Act, by allegedly failing to commence a condition audit within 3 months of commencing service in any of the classes of support that require certification assessment and as part of the stage 1 audit, provide the approved quality auditor with revised self-assessment responses against the applicable NDIS Practice Standards.

More specifically, Safe and Care Services Pty Ltd trading as SAFE AND CARE SERVICES PTY LTD is required by 22 April 2026 to take action to engage an approved quality auditor to complete a condition audit in accordance with conditions of registration imposed under section 73G section of the National Disability Insurance Scheme Act 2013 and by 27 June 2026 to provide the NDIS Commission a copy of the completed conditional audit report.The compliance notice was issued on the basis that a delegate of the Commissioner was aware of information that suggests Safe and Care Services Pty Ltd trading as SAFE AND CARE SERVICES PTY LTD, has contravened section 73J of the NDIS Act, by allegedly failing to commence a condition audit within 3 months of commencing service in any of the classes of support that require certification assessment and as part of the stage 1 audit, provide the approved quality auditor with revised self-assessment responses against the applicable NDIS Practice Standards.

More specifically, Love Supporting Care Pty Ltd trading as Love Supporting Care is required by 22 April 2026 to take action to engage an approved quality auditor to complete a condition audit in accordance with conditions of registration imposed under section 73G section of the National Disability Insurance Scheme Act 2013 and by 27 June 2026 to provide the NDIS Commission a copy of the completed conditional audit report.The compliance notice was issued on the basis that a delegate of the Commissioner was aware of information that suggests Love Supporting Care Pty Ltd trading as Love Supporting Care, has contravened section 73J of the NDIS Act, by allegedly failing to commence a condition audit within 3 months of commencing service in any of the classes of support that require certification assessment and as part of the stage 1 audit, provide the approved quality auditor with revised self-assessment responses against the applicable NDIS Practice Standards.

name: DONOVAN, Jade
narrative: On 23 February 2026 a banning order was made under section 73ZN(2)(b) of the National Disability Insurance Scheme Act 2013 prohibiting Jade Donovan from: 1. Providing, being involved or assisting in the provision, to any NDIS Participant, of any supports and/or services under a Participant’s Plan and which: a. involves unsupervised contact with NDIS participants, whether in a NDIS participant's home or elsewhere; and/or b. involves you accessing or receiving a NDIS participant's personal or financial information. In this instance: • 'contact' means face-to face contact, oral, communication, written communication or electronic communication, where you are physically touching the participant, speaking with, or building a rapport with the participant • ‘unsupervised’ means not requiring direct continuous supervision by a supervisor or senior colleague • NDIS Participant means a participant within the meaning of section 9 of the NDIS Act • NDIS Provider means a NDIS Provider within the meaning of section 9 of the NDIS Act, and • Participant’s Plan means a plan within the meaning of section 9 of the NDIS Act This banning order is for a period of three (3) years and takes effect on 7 March 2026 at 5:00pm and operates across all states and territories of Australia.In making this banning order against Jade Donovan, the delegate of the NDIS Commissioner had regard to relevant criminal history offences.

name: Ritesh DUGGAL
narrative: On 23 February 2026 a banning order was made under sections 73ZN(2)(a)(ii) of the National Disability Insurance Scheme Act 2013 prohibiting Ritesh DUGGAL from being engaged in the following NDIS activities: (a) delivering, or being involved or assisting in the delivery of, supports or services to NDIS Participant; (b) making, preparing, submitting or assisting with any claim, invoice or request for payment to the NDIA in relation to any supports or services provider under a Participant’s Plan; (c) engaging in activities that a member of the key personnel of a NDIS provider would undertake, to the extent that those activities relate to NDIS supports or services; (d) engaging in activities that would be undertaken by a consultant for a NDIS provider, to the extent that those activities relate to NDIS supports or services; (e) engaging in activities that would be undertaken by an auditor for a NDIS provider, to the extent that those activities relate to NDIS supports or services; and/or (f) engaging in activities in a non-service and non-support delivery role for a NDIS provider, to the extent that those activities have a direct effect on the provision of NDIS funded supports or services to NDIS Participant. This banning order takes effect on 5.00pm AEDT on 6 March 2026 for a permanent period and operates across all States and Territories of Australia.

name: Raymond Andrew Robert MANDERSON
narrative: On 13 February 2026, a permanent banning order was made under section 73ZN(2)(a)(iii) of the National Disability Insurance Scheme Act 2013 (Cth) restricting and prohibiting Raymond Andrew Robert MANDERSON from engaging in the below specified activities permanently:Delivering supports or services to NDIS funded participants.Engaging in activities that a member of key personnel of a NDIS provider would undertake, to the extent that those activities relate to NDIS supports or services.Engaging in activities that would be undertaken by a consultant for a NDIS provider, to the extent that those activities relate to NDIS supports or services.Engaging in activities that would be undertaken by an auditor for a NDIS provider, to the extent that those activities relate to NDIS supports or services.Engaging in activities in a non-service and non-support delivery role for a NDIS provider, to the extent that those activities have a direct effect on the provision of NDIS funded supports or services to people with disability in the NDIS.This banning order is permanent and takes effect on 27 February 2026 at 5.00pm AEST and operates across all States and Territories of Australia.

name: Christine Coop
narrative: On 27 August 2025 a permanent banning order was made under section 73ZN(1)(a)(i) of the National Disability Insurance Scheme Act 2013 (Cth), effective on 19 September 2025 at 5.00pm across all States and Territories of Australia. On 20 February 2026, the banning order was varied under section 100 of the NDIS Act, permanently prohibiting Ms Christine Coop from engaging in the provision of NDIS supports and services to people with disability in the National Disability Insurance Scheme (NDIS), including: a) Providing or being involved or assisting in the provision, to any NDIS Participant, of any support or supports under a Participant’s Plan; b) Providing or being involved or assisting in the provision, to any NDIS Participant, of any service or services under a Participant’s Plan;c) Engaging in any work or providing or performing any service or services (whether paid or unpaid), for or on behalf of any NDIS Provider, which may occasion any personal contact between you and a NDIS Participant. Further information: The banning order was made on the basis that a delegate of the Commissioner reasonably believes that Christine Coop contravened section 73V of the NDIS Act by, in connection with providing NDIS supports and services, “failing to provide supports and services in a safe and competent manner with care and skill”; and by “failing to take all reasonable steps to prevent and respond to all forms of violence against, and exploitation, neglect and abuse of people with disability.”, as required under section 6(1)(d) of the NDIS (Code of Conduct) Rules. This variation of the banning order is effective from 5:00pm on 25 February 2026 and remains permanently in effect across all States and Territories of Australia.

name: Ryan Nugara
narrative: On 17 December 2024 a banning order was made under section 73ZN(2)(a)(iii) of the National Disability Insurance Scheme Act 2013. narrative: On 10 February 2026 a banning order was made under section 73ZN(2)(a)(i) of the National Disability Insurance Scheme Act 2013 prohibiting Jerelyn Temple from being involved in the provision of supports or services to NDIS participants.Specifically, the order prohibits Jerelyn Temple from being engaged in the following NDIS activities: a) Provision of any support or supports under a Participant’s Plan. b) Provide or be involved or assist in the provision, to any NDIS Participant, of any service or services under a Participant’s Plan. c) Engage in any work or provide or perform any service or services (whether paid or unpaid), for or on behalf of any NDIS Provider, which may occasion any personal contact between you and an NDIS Participant. Personal contact refers to direct interaction between persons, which includes (but is not limited to) bodily contact with another person, or where persons are in the same physical location where bodily contact is possible.Personal contact also includes (but is not limited to) communications, such as physically speaking to another person, speaking over the phone, emailing, writing a letter, or sending text messages.NDIS Participant means a participant within the meaning of section 9 of the NDIS Act;NDIS Provider means an NDIS Provider within the meaning of section 9 of the NDIS Act;Participant’s Plan means a plan within the meaning of section 9 of the NDIS Act This banning order takes effect on 10 February 2026 at 5:00pm for a period of one year and operates across all States and Territories of Australia.

name: Taufusi Ioane SAUEA
narrative: On 21 January 2026 a banning order was made under section 73ZN(2)(a)(iii) of the NDIS Act of the National Disability Insurance Scheme Act 2013 permanently prohibiting Taufusi Ioane Sauea from: • Provide or be involved or assist in the provision, to any NDIS Participant, of any supports and/or services under a Participant’s Plan and which: a. involves contact with NDIS participants, whether in a NDIS participant's home or elsewhere; and b. involves you accessing or receiving a NDIS participant's personal or financial information. In this instance: • 'contact' means face-to-face contact, oral communication, written communication or electronic communication, where you are physically touching the participant, speaking with, or building a rapport with the participant.• NDIS Participant means a participant within the meaning of section 9 of the NDIS Act • NDIS Provider means a NDIS Provider within the meaning of section 9 of the NDIS Act, and • Participant’s Plan means a plan within the meaning of section 9 of the NDIS Act. The banning order is effective from 5:00pm AEDT on 6 February 2026 and operates across all States and Territories of Australia.

name: Holy Trinity Disability Services Pty Ltd, t/a HOLY TRINITY DISABILITY SERVICES
narrative: Holy Trinity Disability Services Pty Ltd, t/a HOLY TRINITY DISABILITY SERVICES is required to take action to address alleged non-compliance with section 73J of the National Disability Insurance Scheme Act 2013. More specifically, Holy Trinity Disability Services Pty Ltd, t/a HOLY TRINITY DISABILITY SERVICES is required by 20/02/2026 to take action to engage an approved quality audit to complete a mid-term audit in accordance with section 13B of the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Provider Registration and Practice Standards) Rules 2018 and by 30/04/2026 to provide the NDIS Commission a copy of the completed mid-term audit report. More specifically, Profcare Services Pty Ltd, t/a PROFCARE SERVICES PTY LTD is required by 20/02/2026 to take action to engage an approved quality audit to complete a mid-term audit in accordance with section 13B of the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Provider Registration and Practice Standards) Rules 2018 and by 30/04/2026 to provide the NDIS Commission a copy of the completed mid-term audit report. name: Arlie Gibson
narrative: On 14 January 2026 a permanent banning order was made under section 73ZN(1)(b)(i) of the National Disability Insurance Scheme Act 2013 prohibiting Arlie Gibson from engaging in the provision or management of NDIS supports, services or funding to people with disability in the National Disability Insurance Scheme (NDIS) for a period of permanently, including but not limited to: : a. Delivering supports or services to NDIS funded participants; b. Engaging in activities that a member of the key personnel of a NDIS provider would undertake, to the extent that those activities relate to NDIS supports or service; c. Engaging in activities that would be undertaken by a consultant for a NDIS provider, to the extent that those activities relate to NDIS supports or service; d. Engaging in activities that would be undertaken by an auditor for a NDIS provider, to the extent that those activities relate to NDIS supports or services; and e. Engaging in activities in a non-service and non-support delivery for a NDIS provider, to the extent that those activities have a direct effect on the provision of NDIS funded supports or services to people with disability in the NDIS. This banning order takes effect at 5.00pm AEST on 29 January 2026 for a permanent period and operates across all States and Territories of Australia.

name: Felicity BRAZHER
narrative: On 19 January 2026 a banning order was made under section 73ZN(2)(a)(iii) of the National Disability Insurance Scheme Act 2013 prohibiting Felicity Brazher from providing, being involved in or assisting in the provision, to any NDIS Participant, of any supports and/or services under a Participant’s Plan and which: a. Involves contact with NDIS participants, whether in a NDIS participant's home or elsewhere; or b. Involves accessing or receiving a NDIS participant's personal or financial information. In this instance: • 'Contact' means face-to face contact, oral communication, written communication or electronic communication, where you are physically touching the participant, speaking with, or building a rapport with the participant and • NDIS Participant means a participant within the meaning of section 9 of the NDIS Act and • NDIS Provider means a NDIS Provider within the meaning of section 9 of the NDIS Act and • Participant’s Plan means a plan within the meaning of section 9 of the NDIS Act The banning order is for a period of five (5) years effective from 5:00pm 28 January 2026. The banning order operates across all states and territories of Australia. The decision to make a banning order was made having regard to Felicity BRAZHER’s relevant criminal history.

name: Samuella Adama Kaillie Harris
narrative: On 21 January 2026 a banning order was made under section 73ZN(2)(a)(iii) of the National Disability Insurance Scheme Act 2013 prohibiting Samuella Adama Kaillie Harris for a period of three (3) years from: Provide or be involved or assist in the provision, to any NDIS Participant, of any support or supports under a Participant’s Plan and which:involves unsupervised contact with NDIS participants, whether in a NDIS participant's home or elsewhere; orinvolves Samuella Adama Kallie Harris accessing or receiving a NDIS participant's personal or financial information. Provide or be involved or assist in the provision, to any NDIS Participant, of any service or services under a Participant’s Plan and which:involves unsupervised contact with NDIS participants, whether in a NDIS participant's home or elsewhere; orinvolves you accessing or receiving a NDIS participant's personal or financial information. In this instance:‘unsupervised contact’ means:Contact that is face-to-face contact, oral communication, written communication or electronic communication, where you are physically touching the participant, speaking with, or building a rapport with the participant, andWithout the in-person direct observation of another person NDIS Participant means a participant within the meaning of section 9 of the NDIS ActNDIS Provider means a NDIS Provider within the meaning of section 9 of the NDIS Act, andParticipant’s Plan means a plan within the meaning of section 9 of the NDIS Act. The order is effective from 5:00pm AEDT on 28 January 2026 and operates across all states and territories of Australia.

name: All Care Provided

name: Kim Mills

narrative: On 22 December 2025 a notice of revocation of registration was issued to Auspicare Pty Ltd under section 73P(1)(a) of the National Disability Insurance Scheme Act 2013 (NDIS Act). The revocation takes effect from 19 January 2026. Auspicare Pty Ltd can no longer operate as registered NDIS provider, including providing specialist behaviour support, specialist disability accommodation, plan management services, any class of support or service to a person whose NDIS plan is managed by the NDIA and implementing regulated restrictive practices. The revocation decision was made on the basis that a delegate of the Commissioner reasonably believes that Auspicare Pty Ltd has contravened, is contravening, or is proposing to contravene the NDIS Act. In forming this reasonable belief, the delegate had regard to outcomes of an audit undertaken of Auspicare Pty Ltd and which identified a number of major non-conformities with applicable NDIS Practice Standards and which Auspicare Pty Ltd is alleged to have failed to rectify.

name: Sam Griggs

name: Crescent Respite Facility Pty Ltd
narrative: On 29 August 2025, a notice to refuse the application to be a registered NDIS Provider was issued to Crescent Respite Facility Pty Ltd. on the basis that a delegate of the Commissioner reasonably believes Crescent Respite Facility Pty Ltd is not complying with the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Code of Conduct) Rules 2018 (NDIS Code of Conduct) as a Code-covered person and therefore, is not suitable to be involved in the provision of supports or services for which Crescent Respite Facility Pty Ltd has sought registration to provide.The refusal was made pursuant to section 73E(1)(d) of the National Disability Insurance Scheme. The refusal will take effect 5.00pm AEST on 12 September 2025.

name: Sigma SDA Management Pty Ltd
narrative: In accordance with sections 73P(1)(a) and 73P(1)(d) of the National Disability Insurance Scheme Act 2013, Sigma SDA Management Pty Ltd can no longer operate as registered NDIS provider, including providing specialist behaviour support, specialist disability accommodation, plan management services, any class of support or service to a person whose NDIS plan is managed by the NDIA and implementing regulated restrictive practices.The revocation decision was made on the basis that a delegate of the Commissioner:• Reasonably believes that Sigma SDA Management Pty Ltd has contravened, or is proposing to contravene, section 73J of the NDIS Act by failing to comply with the NDIS Code of Conduct and NDIS Worker Screening requirements, and• Was no longer satisfied that Sigma SDA Management Pty Ltd is suitable to provide supports or services to people with disability.The revocation takes effect from 5:00pm AEST on 12 September 2025, across all states and territories of Australia.

name: Ozihub Connect Pty Ltd (formerly known as Sunrise Aged Care and Disability Pty Ltd)
group_codes: 106 assistance in coordinating or managing life stages
115 assistance with daily life tasks in a group or shared living arrangement
117 development of daily living and life skills
narrative: Ozihub Connect Pty was issued a suspension notice pursuant to Section 73N(1)(a)(i) of the National Disability Insurance Scheme Act 2013. Ozihub Connect Pty Ltd cannot operate as registered NDIS provider for a period of 30 days from 5.00pm AEST 12 September 2025 until 11 October 2025, including providing specialist behaviour support, specialist disability accommodation, plan management services, any class of support or service to a person whose NDIS plan is managed by the NDIA and implementing regulated restrictive practices. The suspension was issued on the basis that a delegate of the Commissioner reasonably believes that Ozihub Connect Pty Ltd has contravened, is contravening, or is proposing to contravene the NDIS Act. More specifically, it is alleged that, Ozihub Connect Pty Ltd and its directors failed to comply with the the NDIS Code of Conduct and breached conditions of registration.The alleged conduct presents ongoing and significant risks to the safety and wellbeing of people with disability, particularly in preventing NDIS participants from utilising their NDIS plan funds to access necessary and critical supports and services.

name: Independent Lifestyles Riverina Support Service Pty ltd
narrative: On 25 August 2025 a permanent banning order was made under section 73ZN(1)(b)(i) and 73ZN(1)(b)(ii) of the National Disability Insurance Scheme Act 2013 prohibiting Independent Lifestyles Riverina Support Service Pty ltd from: 1. Engaging in activities of, and as, a NDIS provider;2. Engaging in activities that would be undertaken by a consultant for a NDIS provider, to the extent that those activities relate to NDIS supports or services;3. Engaging in activities that would be undertaken by an auditor for a NDIS provider, to the extent that those activities relate to NDIS supports or services; and/or4. Engaging in activities in a non-service and non-support delivery role for a NDIS provider, to the extent that those activities have a direct effect of the provision of NDIS funded supports or services to people with disability in the NDISThis Order takes effect on 12 September 2025 at 5.00pm AEST and operates across all States and Territories of Australia.

name: Helena Bond
narrative: On 26 August 2025 a banning order was issued to Helena Bond. The banning order is effective on 12 September 2025 at 5.00pm for a period of two (2) years and operates across all States and Territories of Australia. The banning order was made against Helena Bond under section 73ZN(2)(a)(i) of the NDIS Act, restricting them from:providing or personally being involved in the provision, to any NDIS participant, of any supports or services under a participant’s plan; orengaging in any work or providing or performing any supports or services (whether paid or unpaid), for or on behalf of any NDIS Provider.

name: Jimmy KOUFOS
narrative: On 27 August 2025, a banning order was made under section 73ZN(2)(a)(iii) of the National Disability Insurance Scheme Act 2013 prohibiting Jimmy Koufos from providing or managing NDIS supports, services or funding to people with disability in the National Disability Insurance Scheme (NDIS), including but not limited to undertaking the following activities: engaging in activities that a member of the key personnel of an NDIS provider would undertake, to the extent that those activities relate to NDIS supports or services;engaging in activities that would be undertaken by a consultant for an NDIS provider, to the extent that those activities relate to NDIS supports or services;engaging in activities that would be undertaken by an auditor for an NDIS provider, to the extent that those activities relate to NDIS supports or services;engaging in activities in a non-service and non-support delivery role for an NDIS provider, the extent that those activities have a direct effect on the provision of NDIS funded supports or service to people with disability in the NDIS.providing or being involved or assisting in the provision, to any NDIS participant, of any support or supports under a participant’s plan;providing or being involved or assisting in the provision, to any NDIS participant, of any service or services under a participant’s plan;engaging in any work or providing or performing any service or services (whether paid or unpaid), for or on behalf of any NDIS provider, which may occasion any personal contact between you and an NDIS participant.This Order takes effect on 12 September at 5.00pm AEST, for a period of two (2) years and operates across all States and Territories of Australia

name: One Connection Disability Services Pty Ltd
narrative: On 1 September 2025, a permanent banning order was made under section 73ZN(1)(b)(iii) of the National Disability Insurance Scheme Act 2013. The Banning Order permanently prohibits and restricts One Connection Disability Services Pty Ltd from being engaged in the following NDIS activities: engaging in any activities that would be delivering support and services to NDIS funded participants; engaging in activities that an NDIS provider would undertake, to the extent that those activities relate to NDIS supports or services; engaging in activities that would be undertaken as a consultant, to the extent that those activities relate to NDIS supports or services; engaging in activities that would be undertaken as an auditor for an NDIS provider, to the extent that those activities relate to NDIS supports or services; and engaging in activities in a non-service and non-support delivery role as a provider, to the extent that those activities have a direct effect on the provision of NDIS funded supports or services to people with disability in the NDIS.This banning order takes permanent effect on 5.00pm AEST on 12 September 2025 and operates across all States and Territories of Australia.

name: Crescent Respite Facility Pty Ltd

name: Prestige Inhome Care Pty Ltd
narrative: On 1 September 2025, a Compliance Notice was issued to Prestige Inhome Care Pty Ltd.Prestige Inhome Care Pty Ltd, operating as a registered NDIS provider, may be contravening section 73J of the NDIS Act by breaching conditions of its registration determined by the National Disability Insurance Scheme Rules (refer to sections 73F(1)(c), 73F(2)(h) and 73H of the NDIS Act). In particular, Prestige Inhome Care Pty Ltd has contravened National Disability Insurance Scheme (Provider Registration and Practice Standards) Rules 2018 (the Rules) and the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Incident Management and Reportable Incidents) Rules 2018 (Reportable Incident Rules).Prestige Inhome Care Pty Ltd is required to take action to address potential non-compliance, including a review of its incident management system, Risk and Human Resource Management processes and the development of a corrective action plan to address identified non-compliance.

name: Leena Kumar
narrative: On 18 August 2025, a banning order originally made on 9 February 2024, was varied under section 73ZO of the National Disability Insurance Scheme Act 2013. The original banning order made under section 73ZN(2A) was varied from a 2-year banning order to a permanent banning order. The banning order permanently prohibits Ms Leena Kumar from engaging, directly or indirectly, inthe provision or management of NDIS supports, services or funding to people with disability in the National Disability Insurance Scheme, including but not limited to:1. engaging in activities that a member of the key personnel of an NDIS provider would undertake, to the extent that those activities relate to NDIS supports or services;2. engaging in activities that would be undertaken by a consultant for an NDIS provider, to the extent that those activities relate to NDIS supports or services;3. engaging in activities that would be undertaken by an auditor for an NDIS provider, to the extent that those activities relate to NDIS supports or services;4. engaging in activities in a non-service and non-support delivery role for an NDIS provider, the extent that those activities have a direct effect on the provision of NDIS funded supports or service to people with disability in the NDIS;5. providing or being involved or assisting in the provision, to any NDIS participant, of any support or supports under a participant’s plan;6. engaging in any work or providing or performing any service or services (whether paid or unpaid), for or on behalf of any NDIS provider, which may occasion any personal contact between you and an NDIS participant.The banning order is effective from 5:00pm AEST 25 August 2025 and operates across all States and Territories of Australia.

name: Step Free Living Pty Ltd
narrative: In accordance with sections 73P(1)(a) and 73P(1)(e) of the National Disability Insurance Scheme Act 2013, Step Free Living Pty Ltd can no longer operate as registered NDIS provider, including providing specialist behaviour support, specialist disability accommodation, plan management services, any class of support or service to a person whose NDIS plan is managed by the NDIA and implementing regulated restrictive practices. The revocation decision was made on the basis that a delegate of the Commissioner:Reasonably believes that Step Free Living Pty Ltd contravened section 73J of the NDIS Act by failing to notify the Commissioner of an event relating to the suitability of its key personnel in accordance with section 13A(1)(f) of the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Provider Registration and Practice Standards) Rules 2018, andWas no longer satisfied that key personnel of Step Free Living Pty Ltd were suitable to be involved in the provision of supports or services for which Step Free Living Pty Ltd is registered to provide. In forming this belief, the delegate had regard to the involvement of key personnel in:NDIS providers under external administration and/or liquidationNDISP Pty Ltd, an entity against which court action has been taken by the Australian Taxation Office, andContraventions of the NDIS Act.The revocation takes effect from 5:00pm AEST on 8 August 2025, across all states and territories of Australia.

name: Valeria Rosita Hypatia Supetran
narrative: On 25 June 2025 a banning order was made under 73ZN(2)(a)(iii) of the NDIS Act of the National Disability Insurance Scheme Act 2013. The banning order prohibits Valeria Rosita Hypatia Supetran from:Engaging in any activities that would be delivering support and services to NDIS funded participants; or Engaging in activities in a non-service and non-support delivery role as a provider or worker, to the extent that those activities have a direct effect on the provision of NDIS funded supports or services to people with disability in the NDIS. The banning order takes on 4 July 2025 at 5:00pm AEST for a period of five (5) years and operates across all states and territories of Australia.

name: Belinda Annette Insall
narrative: On 25 June 2025 a banning order was made under 73ZN(2)(a)(iii) of the NDIS Act of the National Disability Insurance Scheme Act 2013. The banning order restricts Belinda Annette Insall from being involved in any role that provides NDIS supports or services that involve direct contact with NDIS participants, which in this instance means: physically touching a person with disability; or having contact with NDIS funded participants; or building a rapport with NDIS funded participants as an ordinary part of the performance of normal duties whether face-to-face, or via oral communication, written communication, or electronic communication. The banning order takes effect on 4 July 2025 at 5:00pm AEST for a period of five (5) years and operates across all states and territories of Australia.

name: Mark Allan Forrest
narrative: On 25 June 2025 a banning order was made under sections 73ZN(2)(a)(iii) and 73ZN(2)(b) of the National Disability Insurance Scheme Act 2013. The banning order prohibits Mark Allan Forrest from:engaging in any activities that would be delivering support and services to NDIS funded participants; or engaging in activities in a non-service and non-support delivery role as a provider or worker, to the extent that those activities have a direct effect on the provision of NDIS funded supports or services to people with disability in the NDIS. The banning order takes effect on 4 July 2025 at 5:00pm AEST for a period of two (2) years and operates across all states and territories of Australia.

name: Denise Jayne Clissold
narrative: A banning order originally issued on 23 August 2024 has been varied.The banning order made under sections 73ZN(2)(a)(i) and 73ZN(2)(a)(iii) of the National Disability Insurance Scheme Act 2013 (NDIS Act) was varied under Section 73ZO(2)(a) of the NDIS Act, permanently prohibiting Denise Jayne Clissold engaging in the following NDIS supports and services to people with a disability: Engaging in activities that a member of the key personnel of an NDIS provider would undertake, to the extent that those activities relate to NDIS supports or services.Engaging in activities that include the management or provision of accommodation to people with disability in the NDIS.Engaging in activities that include the submission, modification, or cancellation of payment requests through the NDIA’s provider portal or indirectly via third parties (such as plan managers), in respect of people with a NDIS support plan.Engaging in activities that would be undertaken as a consultant, to the extent that those activities relate to NDIS supports or services.Engaging in activities that would be undertaken as an auditor for an NDIS provider, to the extent that those activities relate to NDIS supports or services.The banning order takes effect on 4 July 2025 at 5.00pm AEST and operates across all States and Territories of Australia.

name: Janette Jean Bones
narrative: On 25 June 2025, a banning order was made under sections 73ZN(2)(a)(iii) and 73ZN(2)(b) of the National Disability Insurance Scheme Act 2013. The banning order specifically prohibits Janette Jean Bones from:1. Providing any supports or services to NDIS participants; and 2. Being involved in the provision, management, or administration of any NDIS supports or services. This order takes effect on 4 July 2025 at 5:00pm ACST, for a period of five (5) years and operates across all states and territories of Australia.

name: Nancy Jonah
narrative: On 19 June 2025, a banning order was issued to Nancy Jonah under sections 73ZN(2)(a)(i) and (iii) of the National Disability Insurance Scheme Act 2013. The banning order permanently prohibits Nancy Jonah from:1. engaging in activities that a member of the key personnel of a National DisabilityInsurance Scheme (NDIS) provider would undertake, to the extent that those activities relate to NDIS supports or services;2. engaging in activities that would be undertaken by a consultant for a NDIS provider, to the extent that those activities relate to NDIS supports or services;3. engaging in activities that would be undertaken by an auditor for a NDIS provider, to the extent that those activities relate to NDIS supports or services;4. engaging in activities in a non-service and non-support delivery role for a NDIS provider, to the extent that those activities have a direct effect on the provision of NDIS funded supports or services to people with disability in the NDIS;5. engaging in the provision or management of NDIS supports, services or funding to people with disability in the NDIS.This Order takes effect on 2 July 2025 at 5.00 pm AEST and operates across all states and territories of Australia.

name: Hope N Faith Care Pty Ltd
narrative: On 19 June 2025, a banning order was issued to Hope N Faith Care Pty Ltd under sections 73ZN (1)(a) of the National Disability Insurance Scheme Act 2013. The banning order permanently prohibits Hope N Faith Care Pty Ltd from: 1. engaging in activities that would be undertaken by a consultant for a NDIS provider, tothe extent that those activities relate to NDIS supports or services;2. engaging in activities that would be undertaken by an auditor for a NDIS provider, tothe extent that those activities relate to NDIS supports or services;3. engaging in activities in a non-service and non-support delivery role for a NDIS provider,to the extent that those activities have a direct effect on the provision of NDIS fundedsupports or services to people with disability in the NDIS;4. engaging in the provision or management of NDIS supports, services or funding to peoplewith disability in the NDIS.This Order takes effect on 2 July 2025 at 5.00 pm AEST and operates across all states and territories of Australia.

name: Sunnyfield
narrative: On 2 July 2025, a compliance notice was issued to Sunnyfield under section 73ZM of the National Disability Insurance Scheme Act 2013.The notice requires Sunnyfield to take certain actions in order to address possible non-compliance with section 20(2) of the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Incident Management and Reportable Incidents) Rules 2018.

name: Araluen Centre Pty Ltd
narrative: On 2 July 2025, a compliance notice was issued to Araluen Centre Pty Ltd under section 73ZM(1)(b) of the National Disability Insurance Scheme Act 2013 (NDIS Act) on the basis that a delegate of the Commissioner reasonably believes that Araluen Centre Pty Ltd has contravened section 73F(1)(c) of the NDIS Act by allegedly failing to comply with a condition of registration relating to the notification of reportable incidents. The notice requires Araluen Centre Pty Ltd to take certain action to address non‐compliance with section 73F of the NDIS Act.

name: Prime Disability Support (Insite Care)
narrative: On 2 July 2025, two compliance notices were issued to Prime Disability Support under section 73ZM(1)(a) of the National Disability Insurance Scheme Act 2013. The notices require Prime Disability Support to take certain actions to address non-compliance with Section 73J of the NDIS Act 2013, specifically around failures to comply with the requirements of Section 73F(2)(c) and provisions of the Restrictive Practices Rules and the Reportable Incident Rules.

name: Hope N Faith Care Pty Ltd
narrative: On 19 June 2025, a notice of revocation of registration was issued to Hope N Faith Care Pty Ltd on the basis that a delegate of the Commissioner reasonably believes that Hope N Faith Care Pty Ltd has contravened section 73J and 73V of the NDIS Act.The revocation takes effect from 5:00pm AEDT on 02 July 2025.

name: Estia Foundation of Australia
narrative: On 1 July 2025, a compliance notice were issued to Estia Foundation of Australia under section 73ZM(1)(b) of the National Disability Insurance Scheme Act 2013. The notices require Estia Foundation of Australia to take certain actions to address non-compliance with Section 73J of the NDIS Act 2013, specifically around failures to comply with the requirements of Section 73F(2)(c). It is alleged that Estia failed to achieve the standard for Governance and Operational Management by failing to demonstrate that perceived and actual conflicts of interest were proactively managed.

name: Braydon Hamilton (Brayden Hamilton)
narrative: On 16 June 2025, a banning order was made under 73ZN(2)(a)(iii) of the National Disability Insurance Scheme Act 2013 prohibiting Braydon Hamilton, also known as Brayden Hamilton, from being involved in any of the following activities:1. Provide or be involved or assist in the provision, to any NDIS Participant, of any support or supports under a Participant’s Plan.2. Provide or be involved or assist in the provision, to any NDIS Participant, of any service or services under a Participant’s Plan.3. Engage in any work or provide or perform any service or services (whether paid or unpaid), for or on behalf of any NDIS Provider, which may occasion any personal contact between you and an NDIS Participant.The banning order is effective on 30 June 2025 at 5:00pm (AEST) for a period of three (3) years and operates across all States and Territories of Australia.

name: Tracey Leanne Murray
narrative: On 20 June 2025 a banning order was made under 73ZN(2)(b) of the NDIS Act of the National Disability Insurance Scheme Act 2013. The banning order prohibits Tracey Leanne Murray from: being solely responsible for the provision of any NDIS supports or services to NDIS participants; and having unsupervised contact with NDIS participants as part of the provision of NDIS supports or services. In this instance: Contact includes physical contact, face to face contact, oral communication, written communication and electronic communication; and Supervision means direct and in-person observation. The banning order takes effect on 30 June 2025 at 5:00pm AEST for a period of four (4) years and operates across all states and territories of Australia.
